context: Add a data-provenance / bounded-scale dimension to the sweep: detect a generator vs a downloader/manifest source, and detect a benchmark that rejects scales other than 1.0, then report those as not-cheaply-gateable with the reason rather than gateable. Regenerate the committed report so the campaign dispatch matches reality.
description: _project/scripts/cross_surface_applicability_sweep.py decides gateability from DataFrame/SQL query-id overlap ALONE. It does not model how a benchmark acquires data or whether it supports a bounded scale, so it reports joinorder as 'gateable' when JoinOrderBenchmark.__init__ raises for any scale_factor != 1.0 ('joinorder now uses canonical IMDb 2013 data and accepts only scale_factor=1.0; use joinorder_synthetic for scaled synthetic smoke-test data') and fetches its data via data_manifest.toml. Wiring it as the report directs would drag a full canonical dataset fetch into routine PRs, violating the gate campaign's own anti-pattern that each gate be one cheap bounded cell. joinorder_synthetic is that benchmark's scaled stand-in and is ALREADY CI-enforced, so joinorder is not really an uncovered gap. flightdata is unaffected: its downloader synthesizes below SF=0.1. The report is the campaign's dispatch document, so an over-optimistic 'gateable' count sends the next session to build something that cannot land.

preserves.behavior: flightdata stays classified gateable: it synthesizes offline below SF=0.1

verifications.description: joinorder is no longer reported as gateable
verifications.expected: exit 0 once corrected; on an unfixed tree the row says gateable and this exits 1
exit 0 and joinorder is not classified as a cheap gateable gap
